implReport.summary: The human-event warning card no longer makes hours loud. Run on 8 hand-over runs, human cards went from 31-66 per 6 game days to 0-11. They fell from 911-1885 s on screen to 0-38 s, and the longest card from 254 s to 5 s. Human cards made 32-76 loud hours per run before and none after. With only people, predators, rivals and major threats counted, every trailing 3-game-day window is quiet at 0.94-1.00 (needs 0.60), and at 1.00 over four whole games to winter, including Gentle and Harsh. With all alerts counted, the share is still 0.04-0.60 per run and E25 as written is not met. The remaining loud hours are the colony's own standing warnings (food, brood), nest flooding, the heat warning and nest crowding, owned by the colony engineer and the nest/weather owners. The telegraph cues, event frequencies and lethal effects are unchanged.

findings.title: Whole-game 'outside alerts + threats = 1.00' is met trivially: no major threat ever started, and the E25 clause requiring one is not reported
findings.where: test-output/quiet-time/long/whole-*.json (threats.started = 0 in all 4); src/sim/environment/human/quiet.long.test.ts:47-49; report §5 and §6 row 2
findings.detail: In all four whole-game runs (suburban-garden Naturalist and Gentle, kitchen-door Naturalist and Harsh) threats.started is 0, and the director refused a threat in every counted hour (blockedHours = blockedByShareHours = 111-154). It refused because the all-alerts trailing share stayed below QUIET_SHARE_MIN + 0.05, which the colony's standing warnings cause. So the 'outsideOnly min 1.00' that the report and the LONG test give as proof that the human/creature side meets I11 is quiet because the director was starved, not shown under normal threat pressure. GDD 05 App. E 25 also requires 'at least one major threat occurred in each Naturalist and Harsh run'. The §5 table leaves this out, and quiet.long.test.ts does not assert it. The report's 'met for everything this task owns' (AC2) is therefore not demonstrated. The human-card change itself does hold up: in the 6-day runs and my high-activity stress run, human cards made 0 loud hours. Fix: report threats started per run and the E25 threat clause as unmet in the whole-game check, and add expect(r.threats.started).toBeGreaterThan(0) for Naturalist and Harsh in quiet.long (red until the colony side is quiet). Reproduction: node -e "console.log(require('./test-output/quiet-time/long/whole-kitchen-door-naturalist.json').threats)"

findings.title: Ease rule ignores its own 'same diagnostic' condition: any lower raise lowers the card
findings.where: src/sim/progression/alerts.ts raiseAlert, lines ~70-76 (cur.diagnosticId = req.diagnosticId runs before `const eased = ... req.diagnosticId === cur.diagnosticId`)
findings.detail: cur.diagnosticId is overwritten with req.diagnosticId before the comparison, so the comparison is always true. Any repeat raise at a lower level with a non-null diagnosticId lowers the card, even when another raiser with a different diagnostic holds it at a higher level. That changes what an alert means, which the spec forbids, and contradicts the doc comment and the report ('a lower level from the same diagnosticId'). The existing test alerts.life.test.ts only covers diagnosticId null, so it misses this. Today it is latent: I found no shared key raised at two levels by different diagnostics (raid-seen via diag-defence is mapped but diag-defence is never published), but any future shared kind will hit it. Fix: save the previous diagnosticId before the field updates. Red test: src/sim/progression/alerts.ease.verify.test.ts 'a lower raise from ANOTHER diagnostic does not lower a card held by a different diagnostic' (expected critical, received warning).

findings.title: GDD 06 §4.5 auto-slow trigger for human-event-warning neither followed nor recorded as a contradiction
findings.detail: GDD 06 §4.5 defines `footfall-warning` -> `human-event-warning` (warning) as 'human footsteps warning active within 120 BU of a trail or entrance'. The implementation raises the card only for a player ant on the surface within footprint + 60 mm of an impact due within 3 s. The task spec asks for the narrower rule, which is defensible, but the report cites only GDD 04 §15.3 and GDD 08 and never records the GDD 06 rule. One effect: a footstep pass over an entrance on sand or loam (block chance 0.5, GDD 04 §15.4) with every ant inside now never warns. The old warn() also needed exposed surface ants, so this is not a regression; it is an unrecorded contradiction for the integrator.

findings.title: A card refused by the site's cooldown leaves no record, and a long event raises several cards
findings.detail: Calling alertRefusal first avoids a log line every 5 ticks, but it also drops raiseAlert's 'alert.cooldown' event-log entry. An ant in the path of a later stripe or step within a game hour gets no card and leaves no record (the spec asks for 'the journal keeping the record'). Also, with the 5 s cap and 1 h cooldown, a mowing run that spans 10 clock hours can raise up to about 10 cards, while the spec asks for 'one alert per event'. alerts.test.ts allows several cards an hour apart, but the report does not list this as a deviation. Suggest logging one 'alert.cooldown' line per event and site, and recording the decision.

findings.title: Weak spots in the LONG whole-game test
findings.detail: (a) MIN = {gentle 0.75, naturalist 0.6, harsh 0.4} copies difficulty quietShareMin instead of reading it, although the header says it asserts against QUIET_SHARE_MIN. (b) A missing snapshot makes the case return and pass silently (`if (!out) return;`), so a run without test-output/colony-life/round-4/cache reports 4 passes and checks nothing. Use it.skipIf on the file's existence, or fail.

findings.title: expireHumanAlerts copies the whole alert list every tick
findings.detail: The copy is made every tick while human events run, even when no human card exists. The cost is small (at most 64 alerts), but it is a per-tick allocation in a hot path. Iterate backwards over the list, or return early when no card of the kind exists.
